questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass of $1$ kg is executing SHM. Its displacement is given by $x = 6.0\cos(100t + \pi/4)$ cm. What is the maximum kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
Given $m = 1$ kg and $x = 6.0\cos(100t + \pi/4)$ cm.

Comparing with the standard equation of SHM $x = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$, we get:

$A = 6.0$ cm $= 0.06$ m

$\omega = 100$ rad/s

The maximum velocity of the particle is given by $v_{max} = A\omega$.

$v_{max} = 0.06 \times 100 = 6$ m/s

The maximum kinetic energy is given by $K_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv_{max}^2$.

$K_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (6)^2 = 18$ J

Answer: $18$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a particle executing simple harmonic motion (SHM), at its mean position
options: velocity is zero and acceleration is maximum.
velocity is maximum and acceleration is zero,
both velocity and acceleration are maximum.
both velocity and acceleration are zero.
questions.solution:
We know that velocity $v$ and acceleration of a particle in SHM.
$v=\omega \sqrt{A^2-y^2}$ and $a=-\omega^2 y\therefore$ At mean position, $y=0\therefore \quad v=\omega \sqrt{A^2-0}\Rightarrow \quad v_{\max }=\omega A$ and $a=0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A block of mass $m$ is connected to a light spring of force constant $k$. The system is placed inside a damping medium of damping constant $b$. The instantaneous values of displacement, acceleration and energy of the block are $x, a$ and $E$ respectively. The initial amplitude of oscillation is $A$ and $\omega^{\prime}$ is the angular frequency of oscillations. The incorrect
expression related to the damped oscillations is
questions.solution:
Equation of motion for damped oscillation is
$\frac{m d^2 x}{d t^2}+\frac{b d x}{d t}+k x=0$
Angular frequency is $\omega^{\prime}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}-\frac{b^2}{4 m^2}}$ Displacement is given by, $x=A_0 e^{-\frac{b}{2 m} t} \cos (\omega t+\phi)$ and energy is given by $E=\frac{1}{2} k A^2 e^{-\frac{b}{m} t}$

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by $x=3 \sin \left[2 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$, where $x$ is in metre and $t$ is in seconds. The amplitude and maximum speed of the particles is
questions.solution:
Given, displacement equation of particle executing SHM,

X=3 \sin \left[2 \pi t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right]

Comparing with displacement equation of SHM as $y=A \sin (\omega t+\phi)$, we get
Amplitude, $A=3 \mathrm{~m}$
Angular velocity, $\omega=2 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\therefore$ Maximum speed,

v_{\max }=\omega A=2 \pi \times 3=6 \pi \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $L C$-oscillations are similar and analogous to the mechanical oscillations of a block attached to a spring. The electrical equivalent of the force constant of the spring is
questions.solution:
For LC-oscillations,
$L \frac{d i}{d t}+\frac{q}{C}=0$
Differentiating further it w.r.t $t$, we get
$L \frac{d^{2} i}{d t^{2}}+\frac{I}{C}=0...(i)$
Similarly, for spring-block system,
$m \frac{d^{2} x}{d t^{2}}+k x=0...(ii)$
Comparing Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$m \propto L \text { and } k \propto \frac{1}{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A pendulum oscillates simple harmonically and only if
I. the sizer of the bob of pendulum is negligible in comparison with the length of the pendulum.
II. the angular amplitude is less than $10^{\circ}$.
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution:
A simple pendulum in practice, consists of a heavy but small sized metallic bob suspended by a light, inextensible and flexible string.
It will oscillates simple harmonically, only if
(I) the size of the bob is negligible as compare to the length of the string of pendulum.
(II) the angle between the normal drawn at the mean position and string at extreme point or angular amplitude is less than $10^{\circ}$.
Thus, both the statements are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A magnetic dipole of magnetic moment \( 6 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Am}^{2} \) and moment of inertia
\( 12 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{2} \) performs oscillations in a magnetic field of \( 2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~T} \). The time taken by
the dipole to complete \( 20 \) oscillations is \( (\pi \simeq 3) \)
questions.solution:
Given, magnetic moment, \( M=6 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{Am}^{2} \), moment of inertia, \( I=12 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{kgm}^{2} \); magnetic field,
\( B=2 \times 10^{-2} T \); number of oscillations \( =20 \).
Now, time period of one oscillation, \( t=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{B \times M}} \)
\( t=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{12 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 10^{-2} \times 6 \times 10^{-2}}}=2 \Pi \times 10^{-1} \)
Therefore, time taken by dipole to complete \( 20 \) oscillations is
\( T=20 \times t=20 \times 2 \Pi \times 10^{-1}=20 \times 2 \times 3 \times \frac{1}{10}=12 s \)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle executing SHM has a maximum speed of \( 0.5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \) and maximum acceleration of
\( 1.0 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2} \). The angular frequency of oscillation is
questions.solution:
Given, maximum speed, $v_{\max }=0.5 m s^{-1} ;$ maximum acceleration,$a_{\max }=1.0 m s^{-1} ;$ angular frequency, $\omega=?$
Now, we know $v_{\max }=\omega A \rightarrow(1)$
where A is amplitude of oscillation.
Also, $a_{\max }=\omega^{2} A \rightarrow(2)$
Using Eqs. (1) and (2), we get
$\frac{v_{\max }}{a_{\max }}=\frac{\omega A}{\omega^{2} A}\Rightarrow \frac{v_{\max }}{a_{\max }}=\frac{1}{\omega}\Rightarrow \omega=\frac{a_{\max }}{v_{\max }}=\frac{1.0}{0.5}\Rightarrow \omega=2 \operatorname{rad} s^{-1}$
Therefore, angular frequency of oscillation is $2 \mathrm{rads}^{-1}$

on the right side of $B$ when the strings are inclined at $15^{\circ}$ with $B$
questions.solution:
Irrespective of amplitude, both spheres take same time to reach the mean position, i.e., $\frac{T}{4} \mathrm{~S}\therefore \quad T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}=2 \times 3.14 \times \sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}=2 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle executing a simple harmonic motion has a period of $6 \mathrm{~s}$. The time taken by the particle to move from the mean position to half the amplitude, starting from the mean position is
questions.solution:
Equation for simple harmonic motion
$\begin{aligned} y &=a \sin \left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right) t \\ \frac{a}{2} &=a \sin \left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right) t \\ \frac{2 \pi}{T} t &=\frac{\pi}{6} \\ t &=\frac{T}{12}=\frac{6}{12}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$
